To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) Cdk4 is required for neuron cell death and 2) Cdk4 inhibitors are potent neuroprotective agents.

1) Several Cdk4 inhibitors protect neuronal cells against cell death induced by nerve-growth factor (NGF)-deprivation, 2) Cdk4 inhibitors prevent loss of mitochondrial integrity induced by NGF-deprivation, and 3) Cdk4 inhibition prevents induction of pro-apototic protein Bim in response to NGG-deprivation.
Cdk4 inhibitors can protect neuronal cells from death induced by nerve-growth-factor deprivation and by oligomeric beta-amyloid, two insults relevant to Alzheimer’s disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing small molecules to target cell cycle proteins in neurodegeneration.
development of novel neuroprotective agents for AD.
the development of novel Cdk4 inhibitors for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cdk4 is a key player in AD and Cdk4 inhibition is a potential therapeutic choice for AD.

Cdk4 inhibitors are effective in protecting neuronal cells from death induced by NGF deprivation and Aβ and these molecules are potential therapeutic agents to ameliorate neurodegeneration in Alzheimer’s disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cdk4 is activated in AD and its inhibition is neuroprotective.
the inhibitors of Cdk4 could be a therapeutic target in the management of AD.
Cdk4 inhibitors can be used as a novel class of neuroprotective agents and they can be further developed as drugs to prevent and treat AD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cdk4 inhibitors are potent and effective neuroprotective agents.
Cdk4 is a viable therapeutic target for neurodegeneration and that a library of small molecule inhibitors of Cdk4 can be used to screen for neuroprotective agents.
Cdk4 is a promising target for developing neuroprotective agents for treating AD.
